content: 1. Drugs that affect hepatic or intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism should be used with caution when co-administered with voriconazole. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Co-administration of voriconazole with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4, a cytotoxic component of mirvetuximab soravtansine, potentially raising the risk of adverse reactions. Close monitoring is advised. 3. Mitotane decreases voriconazole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 4. Voriconazole increases modafinil levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, but monitoring is still recommended. 5. Modafinil increases voriconazole levels or effects by altering CYP2C19 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitoring is advised. 6. Voriconazole increases mometasone (intranasal) levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Voriconazole increases montelukast levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Monitoring is recommended. 8. Both voriconazole and moxifloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 9. Nafcillin decreases voriconazole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 10. Voriconazole increases naldemedine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects, especially when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 11. Voriconazole increases naloxegol levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of significant systemic exposure and potential opioid withdrawal symptoms. 12. Voriconazole increases nateglinide levels or effects by altering CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitoring is advised. 13. Voriconazole increases nefazodone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Nelfinavir increases voriconazole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 15. Voriconazole increases nelfinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Voriconazole decreases neomycin levels by an unknown mechanism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 17. Voriconazole increases neratinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. 18. Voriconazole increases netupitant/palonosetron levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 19. Voriconazole increases nevirapine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while nevirapine decreases voriconazole levels or effects through the same pathway. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 20. Voriconazole increases nicardipine levels or effects by decreasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Voriconazole increases nifedipine levels or effects by decreasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitoring is recommended. 22. Voriconazole increases nilotinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Voriconazole increases nimodipine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 24. Nirmatrelvir decreases voriconazole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Voriconazole increases nirogacestat levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Voriconazole increases nisoldipine levels or effects by decreasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Nitisinone increases voriconazole levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Nitisinone inhibits CYP2C9, so caution is advised when co-administering with CYP2C9 substrates, especially those with a narrow therapeutic index. 28. Voriconazole increases nitrendipine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 29. Voriconazole increases norethindrone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Voriconazole increases norgestrel levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. Monitor closely. 31. Both nortriptyline and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 32. Both octreotide and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 33. Both ofloxacin and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Both olanzapine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Voriconazole increases olaparib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 36. Voriconazole increases oliceridine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. If co-administration is required, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be needed. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 37. Both olodaterol (inhaled) and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 38. Voriconazole increases omaveloxolone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects emerge. 39. Voriconazole increases ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Both ondansetron and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when used with other QT-prolonging medications, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 41. Both osilodrostat and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 42. Both osimertinib and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If no alternative treatment exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 43. Voriconazole increases ospemifene levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Oxaliplatin increases voriconazole levels or effects through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Oxcarbazepine decreases voriconazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor. Oxcarbazepine increases voriconazole levels or effects by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 46. Voriconazole increases oxybutynin levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 47. Voriconazole increases oxycodone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Oxycodone dose reduction may be warranted when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 48. Both ozanimod and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, ozanimod treatment should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 49. Voriconazole increases paclitaxel levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 50. Voriconazole increases pacritinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 51. Voriconazole increases palbociclib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 52. Both paliperidone and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Voriconazole increases palovarotene levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Voriconazole increases panobinostat levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat is known to significantly prolong the QT interval, and its prescribing information states that use with QT-prolonging drugs is not recommended. 55. Voriconazole increases pantoprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Voriconazole increases parecoxib levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 57. Voriconazole increases paricalcitol levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Voriconazole decreases paromomycin levels by an unknown mechanism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 59. Both paroxetine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Both pasireotide and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 61. Voriconazole increases pazopanib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
